relevance_note: Single-centre cohort of 34 Egyptian LAD-I patients with per-patient Table 1 and named ITGB2 variants, e.g. "P17 showed a homozygous deletion c.1848delC".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand. Table 1 (patients as rows, label column "Patient’s No", P1-P34; "#" after P33/P34 marks siblings per legend) was transcribed by a short Python script in my scratch directory; I checked the parsed label, sex, onset, diagnosis, umbilical, skin, other-presentation and outcome cells against the table for all 34 rows. Spans for table values are the row text from the label through the cell. Age columns are in months per the headers "Age at onset (m)" and "Age at diagnosis (m)"; original-text values are the bare cell numbers and ISO values use months (fractional where printed). Outcome ages: alive -> age at last evaluation, died -> deceased_age, per the legend; "lost to follow up" -> vital status not reported. Consanguinity "+" taken as yes; "-" left not reported (text says only "not known to be consanguineous") except P1, stated as "non-consanguineous parents". The legend does not define "-" in any column, so "-" cells are not reported; "No" in "Umbilical stump disease" (defined in text as delayed falling of the umbilical stump &/or omphalitis) excludes both checklist items; "Yes" there and "Yes" for "Skin and soft tissue disease" (a composite including rash, ulcers, pyoderma gangrenosum, thrush) map to no checklist item. Checklist mapping: FTT->failure to thrive; pneumonia->lower respiratory tract infection; OM->otitis media; oral thrush->fungal infections; periodontitis->periodontitis or gingivitis; meningitis->meningitis; orbital cellulitis->skin or soft tissue infections; "enteropathy" mapped to colitis/GI inflammatory disease only for P28-P30, whom the Discussion names as having autoinflammatory enteropathy. Group statements used: "all patients" for leukocytosis, neutrophilia, CD18/CD11b deficiency, Egyptian origin, LAD-I label, IUIS/ESID criteria; "All patients showed homozygous phenotype except P1" for zygosity of genotyped patients; P28-P30 named group; "Patient 26 and two of her siblings" named group. Affected deceased siblings from the "Affected Sibs" column are included as relatives (labels brother/sister of Pn from the sex symbols; P14's two sisters numbered in order of mention, died at 2 and 10 m respectively as printed "2&10 m"; the twins are listed under both P33 and P34 and recorded once as twin brother/sister of P33). Causes printed as "X/sepsis" were read as both X and sepsis observed. A third sibling of P26 (sex not stated) comes only from the Discussion. Four prenatally tested fetuses (siblings of P5 x2, P10, P23) are included; wild-type fetuses have no variant rows. Variant-to-person links: protein HGVS was attached to a patient's cDNA only where the patient sentence names both amino acids and the position and the variant list prints the matching p. string (P8, P12, P14, P17, P18, P19, P28; P1 directly); not attached for P4, P11, P24 (only a truncation position is given). P5, P15, P23 are listed as having previously reported variants but no variant is printed for them: rows kept as "not reported". P10's own variant is not stated (only the fetus's p.G284S); P5's own variant is not stated (fetus is a carrier of p.Gly169Arg); not inferred. Transcript NM_000211.5 is the stated reference sequence for sequencing and is given for printed cDNA variants. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) P4, P11, P14, P18, P19, P24 and P28 variants are called novel but the same sentence set says these patients' variants were previously reported by the centre [10]; "novel" therefore not recorded as a classification. (2) P26's sister: Table 1 "Died-1y", Discussion "died before the age of 1 year" (the Discussion sib was not linked to the table sister for features). (3) P26 and two siblings diagnosed "at the ages of 12, 5 and 13 years, respectively", but which sibling was 5 vs 13 is not stated, so age at diagnosis left not reported for both siblings. (4) P33 is called the family's "first offspring" while Table 1 lists twin siblings of P33/P34 who died at 7 days. (5) Results says 29 consanguineous plus 4 non-consanguineous families (33) and Discussion "88%" consanguineous; P1 "non-consanguineous". (6) Abstract says 58% died in the first 2 years; Results says P1, P13, P16 died later. No stacked " / " cells in this paper.
